Entering Monday night's home game against the Los Angeles Chargers , the Baltimore Ravens are still technically in the AFC playoff picture with a 4-5 record, but they don't have much margin for error remaining. At this stage of the season, any one loss will feel devastating if Baltimore is to sneak into the AFC postseason field. Unfortunately for the Ravens, they're going to have to manage that Herculean task without their best player.
 Two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, who broke and dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand during a loss to the Buffalo Bills two weeks ago, is out for the foreseeable future after undergoing surgery . That means the Ravens are turning to competent journeyman Jacoby Brissett, whom they made a move for before the NFL trade deadline , in an effort to keep their 2026 season alive.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Woof. No disrespect to Brissett, but that's not good.
 At this point, Brissett's mission is to keep the Ravens afloat just enough so they can justify bringing Jackson back in early winter to finish a playoff push. Given the nature of Jackson's injury, mid to late December is when we can probably expect to see him play again, if we will at all. After all, I don't imagine the Ravens will bring Jackson back and risk his long-term health for a team firmly out of the playoff race.
 If the Ravens are still very much alive by then, don't be surprised to see him return for the final 2-3 games on Baltimore's schedule.
